extraction: User-authorized black-only extraction: retain generated pixels with alpha >=16, max RGB channel <=128 and channel spread <=28; bake near-black RGB(7,7,8), preserve alpha and clear all other pixels. The rear layer additionally clears a circular opening of radius (1.04/1.85) times the sprite half-width, with a three-pixel outward feather. No resizing or runtime tint.
rear_generation_prompt: Create a production game sprite, SQUARE canvas, isolated BLACK FILAMENT ART ON A GENUINELY TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND. Use the supplied nebula image ONLY as a style reference for its distant dark filaments, their slightly uneven width, branching, small knots and painted organic texture. Do NOT include any nebula, cloud, star, light, haze or colored background in the output. Subject: the FRONT HEMISPHERE of an immense, extremely sparse, roughly spherical veil spun from black nanofilaments, seen straight-on. It will be composited over a real white dwarf in a game, so several slender threads must cross the middle of the image, while the broad outward curves imply the surface of a loose sphere. The network should look grown and spun, not engineered: irregular asymmetrical long bowing threads with little kinks, variable thickness, tapered wispy ends, small rough knots at occasional junctions, forks, stray hairs, a few slim bundles that divide into finer parallel threads and join again. Match the painted black strands in the reference. About 18 to 24 principal thread paths with sparse smaller branches, huge transparent gaps, more than 93 percent of the canvas completely empty. Main strands vary from hair-fine to a few pixels wide at normal sprite resolution, with localized darker knots; give them MATERIAL CHARACTER and subtle irregularity rather than uniform single-pixel vector strokes. The frontal veil reads as a soft irregular sphere in silhouette, centered and occupying roughly 90 percent of the square canvas, with clear transparent padding at every edge. Keep the network sparse enough that the star underneath remains almost entirely visible. No full perimeter circle, no clean orbital loops, no latitude/longitude globe, no regular ellipses, no geodesic grid, no wireframe, no perfect straight lines, no thick ropes or chitin, no literal spider or characters, no architecture, no glow. Output only black or very dark charcoal painted filaments with antialiased transparent edges. ALL gaps must be transparent, including the center. No white background, no gray background, no baked checkerboard, no shadow backdrop, no sun or planet, no text, labels or UI.
rear_generation_note: The first generated sphere's stronger outer silhouette was assigned to the rear layer; a complementary sparse front layer was generated next.
front_generation_prompt: Create a complementary FRONT-LAYER sprite for this painted black filament sphere. Match the exact organic charcoal-black strand material in the reference: rough little knots, uneven thread widths, wispy split fibers and branching slender bundles, NOT perfect thin vector lines. Output a SQUARE canvas with GENUINE TRANSPARENCY everywhere except the BLACK FILAMENTS. No background of any kind. The reference can serve as the rear/outer layer; this new front layer must be substantially sparser, with about 8 to 12 principal long, irregularly curving paths and a few fine branches, all forming a loose foreground veil across a spherical volume. Several gently bowing filaments MUST TRAVERSE THE CENTRAL THIRD of the canvas diagonally or sideways, so the image has a few organic dark strands crossing its center, not only a circular wreath around an empty middle. Some strands join small rough knots then separate into fine hairs again. Most strands must remain slender; only tiny junctions have a little extra substance. Leave at least 96 percent of the canvas fully transparent. Imply a broad sphere through the strand curvature but do NOT draw a perimeter outline, complete orbital circles, regular ellipses, a grid or regular hoops. Center the entire formation and fit every strand within 8 percent transparent padding around all four edges. The black filaments will be composited over a bright white star in game, so use clean black/dark-charcoal fibers with antialiased alpha and absolutely no colored fringes, glow, gray fog, nebulosity, lights or highlights. No star, sun, planet, spider, characters, text or UI. Do not paint a white or gray matte or a checkerboard. Deliver only a small number of materially irregular black filaments on transparent pixels, in the reference's painted style.
